methodSummary: Behavioral traits combine empirical breed means from C-BARQ with structured breed-guide fields. C-BARQ means are shrunk toward the global mean as a function of breed sample size before conversion to the relative 1–5 scale. Trait weights are multiplied by per-trait data-confidence factors. Health burden is driven primarily by breed median survival in McMillan et al. 2024, with small evidence-based adjustments for brachycephaly and a few high-impact breed-specific risks. The score describes breed-level tendencies, never an individual-dog prediction.

sources.label: C-BARQ Survey dataset, 12,059 dogs
sources.use: Breed-level behavioral means; empirical shrinkage used before conversion to the 1–5 product scale.

sources.label: MacLean et al. 2019, breed differences in behavior
sources.use: Research support for breed-level behavioral tendencies across C-BARQ traits.

sources.label: Morrill et al. 2022, Science
sources.use: Boundary condition: substantial individual variation remains within breeds.

sources.label: McMillan et al. 2024, Scientific Reports
sources.use: Median survival data for 155 purebred breeds in a population of 584,734 dogs.

sources.label: O'Neill et al. 2020, brachycephalic health
sources.use: Small evidence-based health adjustment for brachycephalic conformation.

sources.label: DachsLife 2015 IVDD study
sources.use: Small high-impact health adjustment for Dachshunds.

sources.label: VetCompass degenerative mitral valve disease study
sources.use: Small high-impact health adjustment for Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.

sources.label: Bernese Mountain Dog longevity and causes of death
sources.use: Small high-impact health adjustment for Bernese Mountain Dog.

sources.label: AKC breed scorecard structured mirror, scraped 2021
sources.use: Secondary structured input for grooming, shedding, drool, barking, energy, trainability, openness, protective nature and related breed-guide fields. Cross-check important production claims against official AKC pages.

sources.label: Fadel et al. 2016, working/show Border Collie and Labrador
sources.use: Supports modest line-level differences; line adjustments intentionally small.

sources.label: Sundman et al. 2016, field/common Golden and Labrador
sources.use: Supports separate field/common profiles for Golden and Labrador; effects vary by breed.

sources.label: Battersea working vs show Cocker guidance
sources.use: Lower-confidence practical support for Cocker line variants.

sources.label: English Springer Spaniel Club breed overview
sources.use: Lower-confidence support for distinct working and show types.
